learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will learn to write vivid, structured descriptive paragraphs about people, places, or events by utilizing sensory details, precise adjectives, and logical organization.]
warm_up_hook: 🎨 Think of a descriptive paragraph as a painting made entirely of words. If you do your job right, your reader will be able to 'see' the person you are describing and 'feel' the atmosphere of the place! Grab your word-paintbrushes! 🖌️

lesson_modules.teaching_content: A good paragraph needs structure. Start with a 'Topic Sentence' (the top bun) that introduces the subject. Follow with 'Supporting Details' (the meat and veggies) containing facts, descriptions, and examples. Finish with a 'Concluding Sentence' (the bottom bun) that wraps up the idea.
examples_or_templates: Topic Sentence: 'My grandfather is the most fascinating person I know.'
Concluding Sentence: 'Ultimately, his adventurous spirit is what makes him so special to our family.'

lesson_modules.teaching_content: When describing a person, don't just list their physical traits (height, hair color). Include their mannerisms, habits, and personality. How do they walk? What do they sound like when they laugh?
examples_or_templates: Boring: 'He is tall and has gray hair.'
Vivid: 'He towers over the doorway, his silver hair always slightly messy from running his hands through it when he thinks.'

lesson_modules.module_title: 👁️ Sensory Language for Places and Events
lesson_modules.teaching_content: To bring a place or event to life, use the five senses. Describe what can be seen, heard, smelled, touched, or tasted. This makes the description immersive.
examples_or_templates: Visual: 'The neon signs cast a harsh red glow on the wet pavement.'
Auditory/Olfactory: 'The air was filled with the sizzle of street food and the sharp scent of roasted garlic.'

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ What is the main purpose of a 'Topic Sentence' in a paragraph?
options: To state the main idea of the paragraph.
To list all the sensory details.
To ask the reader a question.
practice_mcq_quiz.correct_answer: To state the main idea of the paragraph.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which of the following sentences uses sensory language most effectively?
options: The pizza was hot and had a lot of cheese.
The bubbling mozzarella stretched from the slice, releasing a rich aroma of garlic and basil.
practice_mcq_quiz.correct_answer: The bubbling mozzarella stretched from the slice, releasing a rich aroma of garlic and basil.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Upgrade this boring sentence: 'The old house was scary.'
subjective_practice.hint: Use sensory details. Describe the peeling paint, the creaking floorboards, or the smell of dust.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write a strong topic sentence for a descriptive paragraph about a crowded local market.
subjective_practice.hint: Make it engaging. Summarize the chaos, colors, and energy of the market in one introductory statement.

activity_or_assignment.title: 📸 The Snapshot Description
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Find a family photograph. Write a 100-word descriptive paragraph about it. Do not tell the story of the day; instead, describe exactly what is in the picture. Focus on facial expressions, the setting, and the mood captured in that split second.

chapter_summary: ⭐ A strong paragraph needs a clear Topic Sentence, detailed Body, and a neat Concluding Sentence.
⭐ Describing a person involves both physical appearance and behavioral/personality traits.
⭐ Sensory language (sight, sound, smell, touch, taste) is the key to bringing places and events to life.
